turn_text: If you are the CEO of a large corporation, most of your multi-million dollar compensation is tied to the price of your stock, and stock prices are largely tied to earnings per share. The easy way is to reduce the number of shares by buying back your own stock. And over the past few decades, America CEOs have overwhelmingly chosen the easy way to the tune of about $1 trillion in stock buybacks a year. The inflation reduction act attempted to address this by imposing a 1% tax on stock buybacks. It didn't really work. For example, since the tax was passed, Chevron announced an additional $75 billion in stock buybacks, and Meta announced a $40 billion buyback authorization even as they were laying off thousands of employees. And so in his State of the Union address, President Biden decided to up the ante by proposing to increase the buyback tax to 4%. That's a great start, but Nick and I think that if you want to make a real impact on stock buybacks, you need to raise that tax much higher or preferably go back to the original rule and make stock buybacks illegal again. Back in 2019, we talked at length with Senator Cory Booker about stock buybacks. And since they're in the news again, we thought it would be a great time to really air that episode. I hope you enjoy listening to it as much as we enjoyed making it.
